athenaeum-revolution.name: Romanian Athenaeum & Piața Revoluției
athenaeum-revolution.blurb: The domed 1888 concert hall in its garden, and the square where the 1989 Revolution toppled Ceaușescu.

footprint.note: ~400 m E-W x 470 m N-S along Calea Victoriei from Biserica Kretzulescu (S) to Str. Episcopiei/George Enescu (N); includes Grădina Ateneului, the Royal Palace (National Museum of Art) façade, Central University Library, the former Central Committee building (Ministry of Internal Affairs) with its balcony, and the Memorial of Rebirth.

structures.name: Ateneul Român
structures.style: Neoclassical with eclectic/romantic touches; architect Albert Galleron (France), built 1886-1888, extended to 1897
structures.massing: Circular drum crowned by a large ribbed dome (total 41 m) behind a temple front: Ionic peristyle of 8 columns (6 front + 2 side) on a high podium with a broad flight of steps; two small lateral corner towers/pavilions

facade.dome_note: dark grey-green metal-clad dome with radial ribs and a small lantern; names of Romanian scholars incised around the dome base (Miron Costin, Gheorghe Șincai, Dimitrie Cantemir, Ion Heliade Rădulescu, Timotei Cipariu)
facade.mosaics: five round mosaic medallions of rulers under the peristyle (Neagoe Basarab, Alexandru cel Bun, Carol I, Vasile Lupu, Matei Basarab) on gold ground
facade.inscription: ATHENEUL ROMAN (sic, old spelling with H) carved on the frieze under the pediment
facade.pediment: triangular pediment with dentil cornice and acroteria (palmettes; winged figures at the corners)
facade.columns: 6 fluted Ionic columns across the front + 1 behind each end, on a stylobate reached by ~10 broad steps
facade.doors: three tall carved oak double doors with glazed iron-grille upper panels
facade.side_windows: tall narrow windows with ornate wrought-iron grilles in the side wings; square windows with star/lattice grilles in the attic of the wings
facade.drum: drum ringed with circular medallions (lyres) between pilasters; names of scholars carved on the frieze below the dome

structures.name: Grădina Ateneului
structures.note: small formal garden in front: lawns, flower beds, gravel paths, benches; bronze statue of Mihai Eminescu (Gheorghe D. Anghel, 1963) on a tall pedestal

structures.name: Royal Palace / Muzeul Național de Artă al României (Calea Victoriei 49-53)

facade.details: long symmetric façade, central portico with paired columns and a pediment, balustraded roofline, tall windows
central cupola, paired columns, statue of King Carol I equestrian stands in front (Florin Codre, 2010, bronze, ~13 m incl. pedestal)

facade.material: white marble pyramid-pillar + dark metal "crown" basket pierced by it
facade.red_paint_note: red paint splash at the base of the crown since 2012 (street artist Keo)

structures.name: Former Central Committee of the PCR (now Ministry of Internal Affairs)
structures.note: Stalinist-neoclassical 1950s building on the east side; Ceaușescu gave his last speech from its balcony on 21 Dec 1989 and fled by helicopter from its roof on 22 Dec 1989

facade.details: colonnaded central balcony on the first floor, long rows of windows

structures.name: Biserica Kretzulescu (1722)
structures.note: Brâncovenesc red-brick church at the south end of the square; exposed red brick with white mortar decorative cornices, two towers

ground.surface: granite slabs (grey/pinkish) around the memorial and statue

vegetation.summary: Athenaeum garden: lawns, low hedges, flower beds, mature linden/chestnut trees; trees along Str. Benjamin Franklin; 42 OSM trees without species tags.

street_furniture: benches (12 OSM; 8 backless benches facing each other around the memorial plaza)
fountains: a row of 7 jet fountains on the south side of the square
athenaeum-revolution.lighting: Athenaeum floodlit warm white with dome uplighting; the museum façade lit; memorial lit from below.
athenaeum-revolution.backdrop: Athénée Palace (Hilton) hotel next to the Athenaeum (west/north), Radisson Blu on Calea Victoriei 63-81, Calea Victoriei eclectic façades; tall Telephone Palace far south.

crowd.typical: Concert-goers in evening wear before 19:00 concerts (George Enescu Festival every odd year in September), guided "Calea Victoriei - Piața Revoluției" tours (most popular Visit Bucharest tour 2024), students at the library, protesters occasionally.

ambient_sounds: Calea Victoriei traffic and trolleybus hum
rehearsal music faintly from the Athenaeum

plaques.title: One leu for the Athenaeum
plaques.text: The Athenaeum was partly funded by public subscription: "Dați un leu pentru Ateneu!" (Give one leu for the Athenaeum!).

plaques.title: The great fresco
plaques.text: Inside, a 75 x 3 m fresco by Costin Petrescu circles the concert hall, telling Romanian history from Trajan to 1918.

plaques.title: The 1919 vote
plaques.text: On 29 December 1919 the Athenaeum hosted the vote ratifying the union of Bessarabia, Transylvania and Bukovina with Romania.

plaques.title: 21 December 1989
plaques.text: On 21 December 1989 Ceaușescu's speech from the Central Committee balcony here turned into the revolt that ended his regime.

plaques.title: Memorial of Rebirth
plaques.text: The Memorial of Rebirth (2005) is a 25 m marble pillar; locals nicknamed it "the impaled potato".

plaques.title: Carol I statue
plaques.text: The Carol I statue recreates Ivan Meštrović's 1930 equestrian statue destroyed by the communists in 1948; unveiled in 2010.

interaction.title: Give one leu for the Ateneu
interaction.desc: Drop a virtual 1-leu coin in the donation box by the steps (homage to the 1880s fundraising slogan) to open the doors and peek at the fresco and the concert hall; on the square, stand on the spot below the CC balcony and hear an archival-style crowd ambience.
interaction.true_to_place: The leu campaign is the Athenaeum's founding story.

photo_angle.note: From the south-east corner of Grădina Ateneului near the Eminescu statue looking north-west at the portico and dome (OSM: Athenaeum centroid 44.441321,26.097215).

seasonal_time_of_day: September of odd years: George Enescu Festival crowds and banners.
21-22 December: commemorations, candles at the memorial.
Spring: blossoming trees in the garden.
Night: illuminated dome is a classic postcard.
athenaeum-revolution.copyright_note: Memorial of Rebirth (2005) is copyrighted (no FoP in Romania): model from reference, do not ship photos as textures.

lines.text: Free walking tour starting here, everyone welcome!
Good day, the Romanian-language group leaves at 11.
Best photo spot is right here, trust me.
Please stay on the pavement, the drivers here don't always stop.
Tips are welcome at the end, it's how I get paid.
Next stop is five minutes on foot.
And this is where the story gets interesting...
"Give one leu for the Athenaeum!" That slogan paid for this building.
Inside: a 75-metre fresco of Romanian history around the hall.
From that balcony Ceaușescu gave his last speech, 21 December 1989.
The next day he fled by helicopter from the roof.
Locals call the memorial "the impaled potato".
The equestrian King Carol I is a 2010 recreation of a statue the communists destroyed.
Kiss your hand... oh, sorry, good day!
lines.orig: Sărut mâna... a, pardon, bună ziua!

lines.text: How are you? Come to see the city?
lines.orig: Ce mai faceți? Ați venit să vedeți orașul?

lines.text: Watch where you are going, young man!

lines.orig: Vai de mine, era să cad!

lines.text: Can't you see I have my shopping bag?
lines.orig: Nu vezi că sunt cu sacoșa?

lines.text: Taking my picture? Let me fix my headscarf.
lines.orig: Mă pozezi pe mine? Stai să-mi aranjez baticul.

lines.text: Send the photo to my grandson, he has Facebook.
lines.orig: Trimite-i poza nepotului meu, are Facebook.

lines.text: In my day there were only old houses here.
lines.orig: Pe vremea mea aici erau numai case vechi.

lines.text: So hot today, what a heatwave!
lines.orig: Ce cald e azi, mamă, ce caniculă!

lines.text: The pension barely buys a loaf of bread.
lines.orig: Pensia nu ajunge nici de-o pâine.

lines.text: The doctor told me to walk every day.
lines.orig: Mi-a zis doctorul să merg pe jos zilnic.

lines.text: Tomorrow I'm going to the market, maybe I'll find good tomatoes.
lines.orig: Mâine merg la piață, poate găsesc roșii bune.

lines.text: These young people only look at their phones.
lines.orig: Tinerii ăștia numai în telefon se uită.

lines.text: My granddaughter is calling, let's see how she is.
lines.orig: Sună nepoata, să vedem ce mai face.

lines.text: God help us keep our health.
Tonight it's Enescu, the Romanian Rhapsody!
The acoustics here are the best in the country.
lines.orig: Acustica de aici e cea mai bună din țară.

lines.text: I've had a Philharmonic subscription for forty years.
lines.orig: Am abonament la Filarmonică de patruzeci de ani.

lines.text: Need help? Can I help you with something?
lines.orig: Need help? Pot să te ajut cu ceva?

lines.text: Wait, I look bad, take another one!
lines.orig: Stai, ies nasol, mai fă una!

lines.text: Put it on Insta, I don't mind.
This is the best angle, trust me.
lines.orig: Ăsta e cel mai bun unghi, crede-mă.

lines.text: Are we going to the Old Town tonight?

lines.orig: Am sesiune săptămâna viitoare, sunt mort.

lines.text: I'm taking a Bolt, not the 336 bus again.
lines.orig: Iau un Bolt, nu mai merg cu 336.

lines.text: Did you see the traffic on Magheru?
lines.orig: Ai văzut ce trafic e pe Magheru?

lines.text: Found a great specialty coffee place here.
lines.orig: Am găsit o cafenea de specialitate super aici.

lines.text: The forecast says rain, but I don't believe it.
lines.orig: Meteo zice că plouă, dar nu cred.

lines.text: I'm off to the university library, law exam.
lines.orig: Merg la BCU, am examen la drept.

lines.text: In '89 the library burned; hundreds of thousands of books were lost.
lines.orig: În 89 a ars biblioteca, s-au pierdut sute de mii de cărți.

lines.text: Have you been to the Art Museum? It's in the former Royal Palace.
lines.orig: Ai fost la Muzeul de Artă? E în fostul Palat Regal.

lines.text: The visitor entrance is on the other side.
lines.orig: Intrarea pentru vizitatori e pe partea cealaltă.
Fără poze cu mine, vă rog.

lines.text: You may photograph the building, not me.
lines.orig: Clădirea o puteți fotografia, pe mine nu.

lines.text: One more hour of my shift.
lines.orig: Mai e o oră din tură.

lines.text: Tickets are sold at the ticket office.
lines.orig: Biletele se iau de la casă.

lines.text: The monument is guarded around the clock.
Please don't climb on the plinth.
lines.orig: Nu urcați pe soclu, vă rog.

lines.text: Excuse me, do you speak French?

lines.orig: Vous pouvez nous prendre en photo ?

lines.text: Thank you very much, it's perfect.

lines.orig: On prend un taxi ou on marche ?

lines.text: It's hot, shall we find a terrace?
lines.orig: Il fait chaud, on cherche une terrasse ?

lines.text: Tomorrow we take the train to Brașov.
lines.orig: Demain, on prend le train pour Brașov.

lines.text: They called it Little Paris, you know.
lines.orig: On l'appelait le petit Paris, tu sais.
Les gens ici parlent bien français.

lines.text: Albert Galleron, a French architect, again!
lines.orig: Albert Galleron, un architecte français, encore !

lines.text: It looks like a little Paris opera house.
lines.orig: On dirait un petit opéra de Paris.

lines.text: Please don't step on the case!
lines.orig: Nu călca pe cutie, te rog!

lines.text: A photo? Drop a leu in the case too!
lines.orig: Poză? Pune și-un leu în cutie!

lines.text: Film it, maybe I go viral!
I played at weddings for thirty years.
lines.orig: Am cântat la nunți treizeci de ani.

lines.text: One more and I take a break.
I study at the Conservatory; I play here for practice.
lines.orig: Studiez la Conservator, cânt aici pentru exercițiu.

lines.text: Got tickets for Enescu? — Yes, in the balcony.
lines.orig: Ai bilete la Enescu? — Da, la balcon.

lines.text: The Revolution happened here. — I know, my dad was here in '89.
lines.orig: Aici a fost Revoluția. — Știu, tata a fost aici în '89.

culture.note: "Bună ziua" (good day) is the safe greeting with strangers; "Salut"/"Hey" among young people. Use "dumneavoastră" (formal you) with older people; elderly men may still say "Sărut mâna" (I kiss your hand) to women as an old-fashioned courtesy. Thank you = "Mulțumesc" or the very common French loan "Mersi".
Bună dimineața (morning), Bună ziua (day), Bună seara (evening); Noapte bună only when parting at night. Pick by the scene clock.

Romanian is a Romance language; young educated people usually speak good English, older educated people often French/Italian/Spanish. Italians/Spanish tourists often half-understand Romanian signs. So bubbles: Romanian for locals with English translation; tourists speak their own language.

Foreign visitors to Bucharest searching online in 2024 came mostly from UK, US, Germany, Bulgaria, Italy, Greece, Israel, Netherlands and France; British searched for Therme, Americans for "Wednesday" filming locations and Romanian food, Bulgarians for Christmas markets/concerts. Use these origins for tourist personas.
Never assume a car will stop at a crosswalk; drivers can be inconsiderate. Locals joke and grumble about traffic, honking, sidewalk parking and buses; keep it good-humoured, never aggressive.

Typical words: mici/mititei (grilled minced-meat rolls), ciorbă de burtă (tripe soup), sarmale (cabbage rolls), papanași (doughnuts with sour cream and jam), covrigi (pretzels sold from street windows). Caru' cu Bere, Berăria H and Hanu' lui Manuc were the most-searched restaurants by foreign tourists in 2024.

Orthodox churches (Stavropoleos, Patriarchal/National Cathedral): people cross themselves when passing, speak quietly, women often cover their heads, shoulders/knees covered; avoid flash and ask before photographing services. Nuns/priests are greeted with "Bună ziua" or "Doamne-ajută" (God help); do not script jokes about clergy.
culture.source: general Orthodox etiquette (no single source fetched from this environment - verify with church staff signage)

culture.note: Romanians are hospitable and insist when offering something ("no" is often treated as politeness and the offer repeated) - vendors/elders can repeat an offer once before accepting a refusal. Respect for the elderly is valued; older men may kiss a lady's hand; handshakes are standard.

Vlad the Impaler is seen by many Romanians as a national hero; some are offended when he is equated with Count Dracula - so locals in bubbles push back ("Vlad Țepeș was one of ours, not a vampire!"). Opinions on Ceaușescu vary; some older people speak of him positively - an elder persona may be nostalgic, others critical; never caricature either.
Avoid lines implying Romanian is Slavic or that Romania was part of the USSR; never confuse Romanians with Roma people.
Unsolicited offers of help/taxis near tourist areas can be scams; locals recommend Bolt/Uber. A vendor/tout persona may push magnets or taxis politely; the player can just walk away.

Communism and Ceaușescu are top tourist interests ("Communism and communist buildings remain at the top of searches"). Locals talk about it with dark irony (e.g. calling the Memorial of Rebirth "the impaled potato"), but lines must stay factual and avoid mocking victims of 1989 (around 1,500 died).

Do not use ethnic jokes (in particular about Roma people) or Dracula/vampire clichés aimed at locals; Dracula appears only as souvenir-vendor patter and as a historical fact (Vlad III built the Old Princely Court).

1 March: mărțișor (red-and-white string trinkets) sold everywhere and given to women; December: "Crăciun fericit!" and the Christmas market in Piața Constituției; winter: "Ce ger!" (what frost); summer heatwaves: "caniculă" (summers often exceed 30 °C).
